44bcbb4f0bb6ca3ca6a74be91d08b24172bf76b0.summary: The report, published by The Hacker News on 2025-04-02, describes FIN7, a financially motivated Russian cybercrime group, as linked to Anubis, a Python-based backdoor that gives remote access to compromised Windows systems. PRODAFT, a Swiss security company, is quoted on the malware's ability to give attackers full control. Anubis is believed to be spread through malspam that entices victims to run a payload hosted on compromised SharePoint sites. GDATA, a German security company, reported that the backdoor can run operator-provided responses as shell commands. The report also says that in…

44528d153681a19a67e9f595deaeaf3dff38e485.summary: WithSecure Intelligence reports late-March 2023 intrusions against internet-facing Veeam Backup & Replication servers, overlapping with FIN7 tradecraft or a threat actor using it. Initial access is likely via CVE-2023-27532, a low-to-medium confidence assessment. The attackers used PowerShell loaders (POWERTRASH, POWERHOLD), the DICELOADER backdoor and DUBLOADER, which side-loads through a Notepad++ binary. They then moved laterally and likely deployed Cobalt Strike. The report judges the scope limited and the goal unclear.

4485a72e8dfe4255f38ac3e0f3f2c549ec82a01f.summary: Mandiant report on APT44 (also called Sandworm), a group it says is sponsored by Russian military intelligence (GRU). It describes disruptive and destructive attacks, mainly against Ukraine, alongside espionage, credential theft and hack-and-leak influence operations run through Telegram personas. Tools include wipers, backdoors and open-source utilities. Several attributions are hedged by the report.

44c6dff1f7f5ad0c568066a6a68ab728cdf6ac3f.summary: Splunk Threat Research Team analysis of Agent Tesla, a .NET remote access trojan in operation since 2014. The sample arrived via a compiled HTML help file and used a PowerShell loader to run the payload in memory. The report maps its behaviours to ATT&CK, covering browser and password-manager credential theft, keylogging, screen capture and exfiltration over FTP, SMTP or HTTP. It also lists detection analytics for defenders.
